Class OrderingStateInspector

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.core.OrderingStateInspector
public final class OrderingStateInspector extends Object
Reads ordering state without an engine.

These are the questions a startup check asks of state left behind by a previous run, and that an operator asks of a stopped process: what is still held, and which topics has this process bound to an identity that no longer resolves.

    • coveredPositions

      public static Map<ChannelId, Long> coveredPositions(Map<byte[],byte[]> latestPerKey)
      Recovers how far each channel was covered as fed-or-never-arriving.

      This is the durable record of a previous execution's read coverage. A start that re-establishes a lost read position must not place it beyond this coverage plus one: doing so would fabricate a read-position report claiming positions were fed or will never arrive when they were simply discarded unread.

      A channel settled on its topic's confirmed deletion carries the engine's fed-to-end sentinel, Long.MAX_VALUE — everything covered. It is returned verbatim; arithmetic on a returned value must not assume it can be incremented without overflow.

      Parameters:
      latestPerKey - the ordering state, as the latest value per key
      Returns:
      per channel, the highest position covered as fed-or-never-arriving
      Throws:
      ParsleyFailClosedException - if a coverage entry is corrupt

    • identityChangedTopics

      public static List<String> identityChangedTopics(Map<byte[],byte[]> latestPerKey, Map<String,UUID> resolvedTopicIds)
      Finds topics that now resolve to a different identity than the one recorded.

      A topic deleted and recreated under the same name resolves to a new identity, which makes every stored position for it meaningless.

      Parameters:
      latestPerKey - the ordering state, as the latest value per key
      resolvedTopicIds - topic name to the identity the broker reports now
      Returns:
      the names whose identity changed, sorted
